missed_issues: Success on bpfix-bench requires passing 'source-semantics checks' written by the authors (§5.1), whose content is not described. The bpfix diagnostic includes explicit 'help:' and 'next action' fix guidance (Figs. 1 and 4). If those checks reward the repair pattern the help text names, part of the gain is from being told the expected fix, not from localization. The 'Proof' column in Table 3 is that check, and it is the largest residual failure for both larger models (16 and 22 of 75 with bpfix).

The layer attribution (source_bug vs lowering_artifact, §4.2) is shown on exactly two hand-picked rejections. No accuracy is reported over the 44 correct-source rejections in bpfix-empirical, so the claim that bpfix 'separates the responsible layer' is anecdotal.

The review lists no conflicts, but the KB has two. 2609.00362 found raw javac diagnostics repaired more Java compile errors than LLM-written explanations, and 2609.22222 found sanitized diagnostics added nothing over a blind redraw. bpfix's gain may depend on how opaque the raw output is (47% EINVAL here), which limits transfer to Java toolchains with informative errors.
Part of the 3B gain is input length, not content: three raw-log prompts overflowed the context window and returned nothing (Table 3, Call column 3 to 0).
Root-cause labels for the 191 bugs (Table 1) come from an unstated procedure with no second coder, yet they underpin the '10 of 12 eBPF-specific' and 'nine root causes per template' numbers.
note: I agree with the review's scores (within one point), verdict, claim grades and all four pattern stances. P17 'supports' is earned narrowly: the same model is given raw versus structured verifier feedback and the structured version wins for all three models, but on the authors' own benchmark with single temperature-0 runs. The review was right to grade the mechanism and retry claims weak; the GLM retry gain is at most 5 tasks. I add that the success oracle may encode the fix the help text suggests, that layer attribution is unmeasured, and that KB Java evidence (2609.00362, 2609.22222) cuts against assuming the gain transfers to javac-style diagnostics.
